title: Enforce data residency for downstream writes (analytics + request/response persistence)
author: Logan Wright
description: Problem: Residency enforcement at request admission prevents cross-region model execution, but we still had paths where downstream side effects (analytics/metering, request/response log persistence, trace exports) could write to a sink configured in a different region than the request’s effective residency region. This undermines enterprise data residency guarantees and complicates evidence collection. This PR adds a fail-closed residency guard for downstream writes. The guard is evaluated using the request’s ResidencyDecision (computed earlier in the request path) and validated against each configured sink’s declared region before any write is attempted. If a violation is detected (sink_region != effective_region), the request is denied with a clear error (machine-readable code), and we emit an audit event capturing the decision and the blocked sink. What changed: 1) Introduced a ResidencyWriteGuard that validates sink destinations for: (a) analytics event stream (usage + latency metrics payload), (b) optional request/response persistence (org setting), (c) trace exporter when configured for customer-visible trace retention. 2) Plumbed ResidencyDecision through RequestContext down into side-effect writers (previously they only had org_id/project_id and a best-effort region tag). 3) Enforced before write: the guard runs at the start of the side-effect phase (still pre-response for synchronous writes; pre-enqueue for async). Violations short-circuit and fail the request to avoid producing any out-of-region artifacts. 4) Added audit trail + metrics: emitted residency.policy_evaluated (allow) and residency.violation (deny) events now include blocked_sink_type and sink_region for these cases; added Prometheus counters: redwood_residency_downstream_write_block_total{sink_type,reason,effective_region} and redwood_residency_downstream_write_allow_total{sink_type,effective_region}. 5) Tests: unit tests for guard logic and integration test coverage for an EU-pinned org with a misconfigured US analytics sink (ensures denial + audit event + no enqueue). Notes/behavior: - Fail closed: if we cannot determine sink_region (missing config / unknown), we treat it as violation (reason=unknown_sink_region) and deny. - We do not log prompt/completion contents in violation logs; the audit event contains IDs, regions, and reason only. - This PR does not add new customer-configurable override behavior; exceptions remain handled via the separate exception workflow and routing override mechanism. Example snippet (pseudocode): `decision := ctx.ResidencyDecision() // effective_region, pinned_region, allowed_regions, decision_id; for sink in sinks { if sink.Region == "" { return deny(RESIDENCY_DOWNSTREAM_WRITE_BLOCKED, "sink region unknown") } if sink.Region != decision.EffectiveRegion { return deny(RESIDENCY_DOWNSTREAM_WRITE_BLOCKED, fmt("sink=%s sink_region=%s effective_region=%s", sink.Type, sink.Region, decision.EffectiveRegion)) } }` Rollout: behind feature flag residency.downstream_write_enforcement (default off). When enabled, we recommend first enabling in staging + a small canary cohort; metrics added in this PR will be used to watch for misconfigurations before broader rollout. Follow-ups: - Make sink_region explicit/required in all sink configs at creation time (currently a few legacy configs rely on implicit region inference). - Extend the guard to object-storage-backed eval/prompt-set persistence (out of scope here).
commits: data-plane: plumb ResidencyDecision into RequestContext + side-effect writers
telemetry: add sink region metadata + enforcement hook
audit: include blocked sink details in residency.violation events
metrics: add downstream write allow/block counters + trace attributes
tests: integration coverage for misconfigured sink region (EU org -> US sink)
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng): "Fail-closed makes sense, but please confirm we’re not emitting any payload fields (prompt/completion) into logs/audit on violation. Also want a stable reason enum for SIEM searches."

Logan Wright (author): "Confirmed: audit event only includes org_id/project_id/request_id/decision_id/effective_region/sink_region/sink_type/reason. No prompt/completion tokens are logged. Added `reason` as a short enum (region_mismatch | unknown_sink_region | decision_missing) and kept the human string in `details` (not exported to SIEM by default)."
Allison Grant (Observability): "Metric names: prefer *_total for counters and include sink_type + effective_region as labels. Also, avoid cardinality explosions: do not label by org_id."

Logan Wright (author): "Updated metrics to `redwood_residency_downstream_write_block_total` and `..._allow_total`, labels are sink_type/reason/effective_region only. Removed the org_id label that was in the first draft."
Caleb Johnson (Tracing): "Please add trace attributes so we can correlate violations in the request span; also ensure we tag the effective region at the top-level span for allowed requests."

Logan Wright (author): "Added `residency.effective_region`, `residency.pinned_region`, and `residency.downstream_write_blocked=true` (when relevant) on the request span. Also added sink_type on the event span only."
Olga Petrov (GRC): "For evidence collection we need the blocked sink type/region in the audit event, and we need the field names to match the audit exporter mapping."

Logan Wright (author): "Aligned field names with exporter schema: `blocked_sink_type` and `blocked_sink_region` in `residency.violation`. Added unit test to validate exporter mapping includes the new fields."
Nadia Rahman (Metering/Audit pipelines): "What happens for async queues? If enqueue fails due to guard, do we still return 200 since the model already ran?"

Logan Wright (author): "We run the sink validation before model execution for requests that have any configured persistence side effects. For truly post-response async sinks, we still validate before enqueue; if a violation is detected late (shouldn’t happen with current ordering), we fail the request and emit audit. This matches the strict guarantee we’re aiming for in the beta cohort."
Marcus Lin: "Approved after reason enum + no payload logging confirmation."
Olga Petrov: "Approved; exporter mapping test is helpful."
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash on 2025-02-11 after approvals; feature flag remains off by default and will be enabled per-canary during Phase 2 rollout.
